### pronghorn.c1: Oversized heart and lungs

Trait ← The thorax houses a heart roughly twice the mass allometry predicts, paired with massive alveolar surface area and high capillary density that shrink oxygen diffusion distance. ← High myoglobin stores buffer oxygen in muscle, letting the animal hold a VO₂ max several times that of a similar mammal without accumulating lactate. ← On the open grasslands where cover is absent, endurance beats sprint: a larger engine sustains minutes of flight rather than seconds of acceleration. ← This matches the F29 template for open-habitat cursorial survival, though rival hypotheses cite leg length or thermoregulation. ← F29

- **Skill:** Sustained Flight (Engage): hold 60 km/h for three minutes across open ground, ignoring rough-terrain penalties and outlasting any pursuer that relies on anaerobic bursts
- **Weakness:** it is built to run past obstacles, not over them: it will not jump a fence and instead crawls underneath, so a fenceline corners it
- **Observe:**
  1. a chase that lasts minutes while the predator gives up in seconds
  2. a barrel chest on legs that look too thin for it
  3. hair snagged under the bottom wire of a fence, never over the top
- **Journal:** It runs from a predator that has been extinct for ten thousand years.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/autoloop-2026-11-18, 2026-11-18)
  - scores: astrobio 10, designer 9, physicist 6, skeptic 7
  - Analogue: Antilocapra americana — elite aerobic capacity and sustained running (Lindstedt et al.); selection context: open plains + historic cursorial predation (Byers 'ghosts of predators past'): as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
  - Analogue: real biology behind this chain: see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own (Lindstedt 1991 [verified]; Byers 1997 [verified])
- **Chain provenance:** council run `autoloop-2026-11-18`; by F, 3, 1

### pronghorn.c2: Dense winter pelage with medullated guard hairs

Trait ← Thick guard hairs pack densely to trap a still-air boundary layer against the skin, where thermal resistance R scales with thickness d and low conductivity k. ← On the exposed continental interior, wind strips that boundary layer, so survival depends on maintaining R against convective heat loss rather than relying on hollow lumens. ← F4’s axial tilt drives the annual solar swing, while inferred continental wind patterns demand a coat that can be shed when the sun returns. ← The moult leaves patchy bare skin in spring, turning winter insulation into a heat trap before the new undercoat fully forms. ← F4, F29

- **Skill:** Winter Coat (Passive): no cold penalty down to -45 °C wind chill and full stamina regeneration while bedded in snow; a distinct blue-ice Overheat meter fills twice as fast under summer sun, forcing shade or water before it tops out
- **Weakness:** between the spring moult and the new coat the fur is patchy, bare skin burns and the Overheat meter runs hot: corner it in open sun at midday, or pen it behind a fence it will not jump, and the winter-proof coat becomes a summer trap
- **Observe:**
  1. a shed guard hair snapped in two showing a fibrous core rather than a hollow tube
  2. it stands rump to the wind while everything else faces away
  3. in late spring the coat lifts in patchy tufts with pink bare skin showing
- **Journal:** A desert coat worn in a blizzard, and a blizzard coat worn in the sun.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/autoloop-2026-11-18, 2026-11-18)
  - Tie -45 °C wind-chill survival to calm-to-moderate wind unless 'bedded in snow' explicitly adds microclimate; pronghorn still suffer extreme exposure during blizzards.
  - scores: astrobio 9, designer 9, physicist 8, skeptic 6
  - Analogue: Pronghorn hollow guard hairs; convergent hollow/filament insulation in caribou (Rangifer) and muskox (Ovibos): as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
  - Analogue: real biology behind this chain: see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own (Blix 2016 [verified]; Byers 1997 [verified])
  - Fix: Tie -45 °C wind-chill survival to calm-to-moderate wind unless 'bedded in snow' explicitly adds microclimate; pronghorn still suffer extreme exposure during blizzards.
- **Chain provenance:** council run `autoloop-2026-11-18`; by F, 3, 1

### pronghorn.c3: Laterally placed orbits with wide interorbital spacing

Trait ← The orbits sit high and far back on the skull, maximizing horizontal field of view to roughly 320° while compressing binocular overlap to a narrow wedge of about 32°. ← This optical geometry sacrifices stereoscopic depth perception for early motion detection at the visual periphery. ← On the treeless plains of F29, cover is absent, so spotting a moving stalker long before shape resolution dictates survival. ← The trade-off leaves a blind sector directly behind and poor close-range depth judgment, forcing the animal to rely on herd vigilance and early flight. ← F29

- **Skill:** Horizon Watch (Control): spots a moving concealed creature at 500 m and grants the party +2 initiative; also reveals a hidden creature's position one turn early, but detection drops to 250 m in scrub
- **Weakness:** the eyes trade binocular overlap for width: it is poor at judging close range and blind in a wedge directly behind, so a stalker that gets inside 40 m from downwind is invisible to it
- **Observe:**
  1. eyes on the flanks of the head with almost no forward overlap
  2. a head that lifts from grazing every few seconds, always the same direction
  3. a sharp snort given at something you cannot see yet
- **Journal:** It watches the horizon so hard it forgets to watch its feet.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/autoloop-2026-11-18, 2026-11-18)
  - 800 m 'concealed ambusher' is generous for cryptic stalker in tall grass; reserve 800 m for obvious motion on open plain; scrub halve detection. Binocular overlap ~32° (ungulate typ.) supports close-range depth weakness.
  - scores: astrobio 8, designer 9, physicist 7, skeptic 6
  - Analogue: Pronghorn — lateral orbits, ~300°+ visual field, distance vision on open shortgrass steppe (ungulate anti-ambush template): as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
  - Analogue: real biology behind this chain: see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own (Byers 1997 [verified])
